chapters.title: Player guide
chapters.summary: Your first session, controls, captures, ranch work and rebirths.

sections.title: Start here
sections.markdown:
Sleep Pets & Chop Trees is a ranch and collection game. Put wild animals to sleep with dart guns, carry them across the brick edge into the hub, and settle them in your enclosure. Placed pets earn Cash on their own. Cut trees with melee tools for Wood, then use both currencies and the required pet to rebirth and open more of the map.

> **Your first session.** Claim both welcome gifts in Rewards. Buy the Dart Pistol for **$5,000** and, when the tutorial sends you back, the Baseball Bat for **20 Wood**. Make your first catch in the Grassland close to the brick path. Keep the first pets in your pen to earn while you explore.

| What you want to do | Where to go |
| --- | --- |
| Catch your first pet | [The tutorial](#tutorial) and [capture walkthrough](#capture) |
| Buy or equip a weapon | **Weapon Store** at the hub. **Upgrade** has per-weapon upgrades. |
| Find a pet you own | **Ranch** for placed pets, **Bag** for stored items, **Upgrade → Animals** for all owned pets. |
| Make more Cash | Fill the pen, place your best earners, claim [Rewards](#rewards), and [rebirth](#rebirth). |
| Make more Wood | Equip a melee tool and [chop trees](#chop), including golden trees. |
| Find an animal or compare pets | [Biome atlas](#world) and [species tables](#grassland). |
| Find a quick answer | [Player FAQ](#faq) and [troubleshooting](#troubleshooting). |

[image:ranch-v7-overview]

**Build used for this guide.** The open Studio place reported version **260**, place **109510233820622**, universe **10774990312**. The loading screen says **Wild Ranch Simulator**. This guide uses the experience name **Sleep Pets & Chop Trees** from Studio. Screens marked _Archived play_ or _Archived Studio view_ are genuine local project images from earlier builds. Use this guide's tables and instructions for version 260.

sections.title: First ranch, step by step
sections.markdown:
The tutorial uses white arrows on the ground, a pointing finger on menus, and a guide dialog. Close a menu with its red **X** if the guide tells you to switch. Follow its prompts in order on your first visit.

| Step | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| 1\. Claim your welcome gifts | Press **Next** on the greeting. Open **Rewards → Missions**. Press **Claim** for **$10,000**, then press the separate **Claim** for **100 Wood**. |
| 2\. Buy the Dart Pistol | Follow the arrows to the **Weapon Store**. Press **E**, use the gamepad prompt, or tap. Open **Guns** and buy the **Dart Pistol** for **$5,000**. |
| 3\. Go to the Grassland | Cross the end of the brick apron. The Grassland starts immediately beyond it. |
| 4\. Take out the gun | Press **2** or tap the gun slot. The crosshair appears. |
| 5\. Put an animal to sleep | Aim the crosshair at a nearby Common pet and shoot until its sleep progress reaches 100%. A normal-sized Deer, Fox, or Boar needs three clean Dart Pistol hits at base power. |
| 6\. Pick it up | Approach the sleeping pet and press **E** or tap **Pick Up**. |
| 7\. Bring it home | Head straight back across the brick edge, then walk into **your own** fenced enclosure. Wait for the capture notification. |
| 8\. Improve the gun | Open **Upgrade → Guns → Dart Pistol** and buy **+1 Sleep DMG**. The first point costs **$540**. |
| 9\. Buy the bat | Return to the **Weapon Store → Melee** and buy the **Baseball Bat** for **20 Wood**. |
| 10\. Chop a Grassland tree | Press **1** or tap the melee slot. Face a trunk outside the hub and swing until the tree falls. |
| 11\. Buy food | Go back to **Food Market**. Open its prompt, select **Cabbage**, then use the green **$1,000** price button. |
| 12\. Feed your pet | Open **Upgrade → Animals → your animal → Feed** and give it one serving. |
| 13\. Buy a pet stat | Return to the animal card and use **+1** on a stat. Finishing the first run pays a one-time **$1,000** tutorial reward. |

**Skip and replay.** Skipping delivers any eligible welcome gifts and puts missing starter equipment in inventory. The completion bonus comes from finishing the tutorial. To review the instructions, use **Settings → Replay** after the tutorial has ended. A replay begins at the weapon step and pays no extra tutorial rewards. First-time tutorial players get protection from direct wild attacks and have storm visuals suppressed. Nearby wild animals are slowed for the first-time tutorial.

sections.title: Find, aim and put a pet to sleep
sections.markdown:
1.  **Pick a target you can bring home.** Early on, work near the Grassland entrance. The biome badge tells you where you are. A target has to be in its home biome, and you need to be inside that same biome when you fire.
2.  **Use an open line of sight.** Equip the dart gun and move the center crosshair onto the animal. The reticle and hit feedback help confirm aim. Terrain, rocks, tree trunks and buildings can stop the dart. The high boundary cliffs are also blocked for capture. Scoped view moves to eye height and hides your character and mount locally.
3.  **Build up sleep progress.** Each hit adds that gun's Sleep DMG to your own progress on the target. Another player's hits build their own bar. The first player to reach 100% puts the pet to sleep. Melee flings a wild animal instead of adding sleep progress. A hit on a conscious animal often makes it flee or charge.
4.  **Reload when needed.** Ammo is a magazine count. Reload a partial magazine with the reload input, or let an empty one reload automatically. The gun's tag or upgrade card shows magazine size, reload, rate, range and Sleep DMG. The current gun uses manual aim.

**When a pet lies down, move in.** Wild sleep usually lasts **45 seconds**. The player who put it to sleep has the first **5 seconds** of pickup protection. After that, the first eligible player to pick it up takes it. The reach starts from a 14-stud setting and is adjusted for animal size and mounting. Fly close enough to get the prompt. A flying pet falls or glides toward the ground when sedated.

**Animals react differently.** Timid and alert wildlife tend to run. Aggressive animals can retaliate after a hit. Aggressive Epic and higher animals can charge on approach. Mystic flyers can dive. At night, wildlife detection distance is 75% of its daytime distance. Ordinary player walking speed is 26 studs per second, so use a clear approach and consider a mount for longer chases.

sections.title: Carry the catch home
sections.markdown:
When you pick up a sleeping wild pet, it rides overhead and the **Bring it home** bar starts. The game gives the carried pet a travel timer based on your distance to your pen, the biome, its rarity and appearance, and how much it slows you down. A heavy roll relative to the pet’s species can slow you more. For the Grassland the allowance is tuned around walking. Later biomes use a pace based on a normal Rare mount from the previous biome.

-   **Cross the brick edge first.** As soon as your delivery is safely across the Grassland-to-hub line, the carry clock stops. The **Safe! Put it in your enclosure** message tells you that you can finish the walk through the square.
-   **Finish inside your fence.** Step into your own enclosure or use **Drop** over it to deliver. An open pen slot places the pet. If the pen is full, delivery stores it, and it can appear in a hotbar slot if there is room. If both are full, make a space before trying to finish.
-   **Keep moving through the wild.** A rival can knock a carried pet out of your hands before you reach safety. A stolen drop has no pickup protection. A player who successfully delivers somebody else's knocked-loose pet can complete the steal mission. Pets in the ranch are protected from theft.
-   **A manual drop starts a ground timer.** A pet you drop outside your pen lands on the ground and stays asleep for at least 15 seconds, or for the remaining carry time if that is longer. It can be picked up again. If it wakes, it runs toward its habitat. Flying drops use the ground below. Leaving the server with an unfinished carry loses it.

**What changes at dusk?** Night helps recovery after delivery and makes wildlife slower to notice you. The carry timer counts down at the same speed day and night.

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| **Protected** | Wait for the short protection window to end if another player sedated it. |
| **Get closer** | Close the gap to the pet or get near it on your mount. |
| **Hurry! It's waking up!** | Head straight for the brick edge. The red bar indicates the final quarter. |
| **Safe!** | Walk into your enclosure and look for the capture notification. |
| **Ranch and bag are full!** | Free a storage or pen slot. Keep track of any pet you are still carrying. |
| **It woke up and ran away!** | A lost catch has to be sedated and picked up again. It bolts during its first few seconds. |

sections.title: Run your ranch and train pets
sections.markdown:
You get an enclosure when your profile loads. The place has six authored plots around the hub. A new ranch has **6 placed slots** and room for **60 stored animals** under normal capture and storage rules. Each rebirth adds one pen slot, up to **12**. Some reward and crate grants can land in storage beyond the normal capture cap.

| Action | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| See your pen | Open **Ranch**. Its counter shows placed animals against capacity. |
| Inspect a pet | Open its card from **Upgrade → Animals**, the Ranch list or the Bag. Check its rarity, traits, recovery, earnings, size, weight, age, XP and upgrades. |
| Place a stored pet | Use **Place** on its card where offered, or hold it and click/tap an open spot inside your fence. |
| Move a placed pet | Use the placement action from its ranch card. Pick a floor spot with room inside your own fence. |
| Store a pet | Use the pet card's **Unequip** action to return a placed pet to Bag. |
| Fill with top earners | **Place Best** sorts pets by base income and fills the enclosure. The currently ridden pet is left alone. |
| Feed | Use **Feed** on the pet card, or hold food and approach or tap the pet. A feeding adds the food's XP. |
| Improve a stat | On the pet card, spend Cash with **+1** or **MAX** where shown. **MAX** stops at the cap or when Cash runs out. |
| Decorate | Open **Ranch → Decorate**. Buy props with Wood and choose one of the six fixed spots. An owned prop can be reused or removed. |
| Sell | Visit **Sell Stand**. Select individual pets or a batch, review the value, and confirm. The sale is permanent. |

**Recovery.** A newly captured pet arrives recovering. It earns half its awake rate while placed and cannot be ridden until awake. Recovery work spans **2 minutes** for a Grassland Common to **90 minutes** for an Enchanted Mystic at daytime base speed. Night runs remaining recovery at **10×** and the permanent recovery perk adds **4×**, for **40×** together. The displayed remaining time changes when the rate changes. A reward or crate pet is granted ready to use. **Wake Now** is a paid shortcut for an owned pet still recovering.

**Training.** Food gives XP. XP opens room for separately purchased Cash stat upgrades. At level 1 you can already buy three points per stat. Each level adds room for three more, subject to each stat's cap. Read [Pet levels and earnings](#pet-math) for the rarity ceilings and exact stat effects.

sections.title: Ride, fly and take a passenger
sections.markdown:
**Ride an awake pet you own.** Walk up to it in the ranch and use **Ride**, or hold it from Bag and click or tap the **Ride** button. Mounting a placed pet moves it out of its earning slot and into the stored/riding state. When you dismount it comes back to your hands. Place it in the enclosure again to resume passive income from that pet.

**On the ground.** Move with the normal controls. Tap Jump for a hop. Ground speed depends on biome, rarity, appearance, mutation, size, weight and Speed upgrades. Jump upgrades affect the jump. Dismount on the ground with the visible button, or the controller **B** binding. **E** is the ranch pet prompt for getting on.

**In the air.** Griffin, Sand Dragon, Dragon and Violet Wyvern can fly. Hold Jump for roughly half a second to take off, or use the **Fly** button on touch. Keep Jump held to climb, hold **Q** or the descent control to go down, or select **Land**. The flight ceiling is about **250 studs of world height**. Biome gates and world edges still apply. You can aim and fire a dart gun in flight when the normal capture checks pass. Land before a driver dismounts. If the animal you are riding covers the crosshair in unscoped gun mode, it fades locally. Scoping can hide the mount and rider on your screen.

**Ride along.** Approach another player's grounded mount and use its **Ride along** prompt. It has one passenger seat behind the driver. You need free hands for a carried catch and the seat must be free. The driver steers. A passenger can leave with the passenger action or Jump even during flight and is placed down toward the ground. A hit on a mount can move both riders. A carried pet and a flying mount need extra space near the ground, gates and trees.

**Mount action.** **R** or **Y** with the gun away plays the mount's attack animation. The riding path triggers an animation. Wild charge knockback and equipped melee strikes have their own combat rules.

sections.title: Chop trees and handle knockback
sections.markdown:
Equip the **Baseball Bat** or another melee weapon. Walk up to a trunk, face it and click or tap to swing. Watch the chips and progress. When it falls, Wood is credited to your wallet and the trunks fly toward your HUD. The starter bat has 1 base Tree DMG, a 0.5-second swing and one-tree cleave. A reference Grassland tree needs six ordinary starter hits. Critical hits and tree size change that count.

| Logging rule | Current build |
| --- | --- |
| Auto Chop | Equip melee and click the **Auto Chop** icon over Rebirth and Upgrade. The green arrow means on. It swings at the weapon's pace when a tree is in reach in front of you. It does not walk you to the next tree. |
| Golden tree | 3% roll on setup and regrowth. Look for the golden sparkle. It pays 5× the tree's usual Wood before your modifiers. |
| Critical hit | 15% chance per tree hit. A critical hit does 2× tree damage. |
| Regrowth / healing | A fallen tree regrows after about 7 seconds. Unfinished chop damage heals after 20 seconds unattended. A regrowing trunk can remain walk-through until the space clears. |
| Shared tree | Players who dealt damage share its Wood by contribution, with a minimum one Wood for eligible contributors. |
| Later weapons | More Tree DMG and more cleave at higher tiers. The first three tools have blade hits only. Starting at Cenarius, a growing crescent can reach trees and other valid targets. |
| Wood boosters | Earn upgrades, rebirths and the 2× Wood perk stack on tree payout. Fractional bonus Wood is rounded by chance across hits. |

**Player versus player.** Outside the ranch safe area, a melee blow can fling and briefly ragdoll a player or mount. It does not take health as conventional weapon damage. Ragdoll duration is roughly **1.6–3 seconds**. After a player's hit ends, there is a **3-second** guard against the next player hit. Body weight affects knockback. If you're delivering a catch, the fastest protection is to cross back into the ranch square. Swinging and tree chopping still work in the safe area.

**Spend Wood on purpose.** Wood buys melee weapons, their four stat tracks, decorations and the Wood part of rebirth. The Shop also sells Wood packs. A larger or later-biome tree takes more work and grants more Wood, so match your tool to the habitat. [Compare the full melee catalog](#melee).

sections.title: Unlock the six ranch tiers
sections.markdown:
Open **Rebirth** to see the exact species your profile needs. It is one Common, Uncommon or Rare from the biome you are finishing. A pet in the Bag also counts. The requirement is saved for that stage. Keep the pet until you rebirth. The progress bar uses the lower of your Cash and Wood progress, and the ready badge also checks the animal.

| Stage | Cash needed | Wood | Pet from | Enclosure | Opens | Slots | Cash / Wood |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1   | $280,000 | 250 | Grassland | Meadow | Savanna | 7   | ×2 / ×1.5 |
| 2   | $4,000,000 | 800 | Savanna | Safari | Snowland | 8   | ×4 / ×2.25 |
| 3   | $20,000,000 | 5,000 | Snowland | Glacier | Desert | 9   | ×8 / ×3.375 |
| 4   | $80,000,000 | 20,000 | Desert | Oasis | Prehistoric | 10  | ×16 / ×5.0625 |
| 5   | $800,000,000 | 100,000 | Prehistoric | Jurassic | Enchanted Grove | 11  | ×32 / ×7.5938 |
| 6   | $16,000,000,000 | 500,000 | Enchanted Grove | Crystal | Final tier | 12  | ×64 / ×11.3906 |

A currency rebirth resets your Cash balance to **0**, deducts the listed Wood and keeps your pets, tools, upgrades, Index and other inventory. The required animal also stays in your collection. A **199 Robux** skip can advance one stage and keeps your balances and collection. Each stage adds a pen slot and a new enclosure style. Each doubles passive Cash and multiplies tree Wood by **1.5×** relative to the previous stage.

### A practical progression route

1.  Fill the initial six slots with catches near the Grassland entrance. Claim the daily calendar and any ready missions or Index rewards.
2.  Keep your required species, buy the melee tool you need for reliable logging and get at least one pet recovered for riding. Spend on upgrades before a currency rebirth if the upgrade fits your next habitat and you already have enough to meet the rebirth threshold afterward.
3.  Enter the newly opened biome. Replace weak earners gradually and keep a fast mount available for the return trip. Check **Rebirth** as soon as you open the next stage so you know which species to keep.
4.  At stage six the **Crystal** enclosure, 12 slots and full multipliers are the final goals. Enchanted Grove itself opens one rebirth earlier.

sections.title: Read the map
sections.markdown:
The world runs in one direction from the Ranch Hub through six habitats. The brick apron is the hub's edge. Follow the landscape through the next gate to advance. If a gate tells you to rebirth, use the [Rebirth panel](#rebirth) and check the required animal, Cash and Wood. Walking, riding and flight all obey the unlocks.

| Region | Opens | X reference | Weather | Landmark cue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Grassland](#grassland) | Start | 556–2,200 | Thunderstorm | Meadows and soil banks |
| [Savanna](#savanna) | Rebirth 1 | 2,200–3,800 | Lightning Storm | Golden grass and rock arches |
| [Snowland](#snowland) | Rebirth 2 | 3,800–5,400 | Blizzard | Snow shelves and pines |
| [Desert](#desert) | Rebirth 3 | 5,400–7,000 | Sandstorm | Sandstone mesas and cacti |
| [Prehistoric](#prehistoric) | Rebirth 4 | 7,000–8,600 | Ancient Storm | Ferns and dinosaur country |
| [Enchanted Grove](#enchanted) | Rebirth 5 | 8,600–10,200 | Magic Storm | Mushrooms and crystals |

The X values above are the server's configured biome checkpoints in studs. Grassland starts at the paved line, **X = 556**. The spacing formula for later gates uses **600 + 1,600 × (biome number − 1)**. Enchanted Grove is the last named region. The broad world boundary extends past its reference interval in places. The side mountains and world bounds constrain travel. Walkable slope is capped at **50°**, and riders ease to a stop near the edge.

### What is in the Ranch Hub?

-   **Weapon Store** sells dart guns and melee tools on separate tabs. The six premium weapon displays around the plaza correspond to the last three guns and last three melee tools.
-   **Food Market** sells pet XP food. **Gear Shop** sells Radars. **Sell Stand** buys animals. Follow the station prompt at the counter.
-   **Top Ranchers** shows ten positions per column for lifetime Cash, lifetime Wood and played time. These are separate from the Cash and Wood balances you can spend.
-   **Feedback** lets you send a short filtered note to the owner. Draft text survives closing the panel during play. The server expects 4–400 bytes of text and at most one accepted note per minute. The hub has a fountain, shopkeepers, lanterns and six surrounding plots.
-   Old archive pictures show named Mystic displays and prices. Use the current crate catalog for Mystic purchases. The hub's current weapon displays are managed separately.

sections.title: Spawns, rarity and appearance
sections.markdown:
Each biome has **12 species** in the same layout of **3 Common, 2 Uncommon, 2 Rare, 2 Epic, 2 Legendary, 1 Mystic**. The ordinary target is **60 wildlife per biome**. A normal refill gives each eligible species its rarity weight. A second selection favors species with fewer examples currently alive in that biome. Epic fills have a cap of **3 per biome**. An unseen portion of the population rotates roughly every 20 seconds, with a larger turnover around dawn and dusk.

| Rarity | Ordinary refill weight per eligible species | How it occurs in the wild | Nominal lifetime |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Common | 30  | Normal refill | No fixed expiry, can rotate |
| Uncommon | 12  | Normal refill | No fixed expiry, can rotate |
| Rare | 5   | Normal refill | 20 minutes |
| Epic | 1.8 | Normal refill under the Epic cap | 15 minutes |
| Legendary | 0   | Scheduled every 3 server hours plus party specials | 60 minutes, with an extension when attended |
| Mystic | 0   | Scheduled every 6 server hours on a +30-minute offset, one active scheduled Mystic max | 60 minutes, with an extension when attended |

The standard Legendary schedule starts at server age **3:00**. The standard Mystic schedule first comes due at **6:30**, then **12:30**, and so on. The clock belongs to that server. A joining player does not reset it. The standard rolls choose a biome at spawn time and regular notices do not tell players the biome. The HUD rotates the countdowns with **roaming now!** while a rarity is active. After the nominal hour, a Legendary or Mystic stays while a player is within roughly **200 studs** or it has been hit in the last **60 seconds**. A due spawn can miss if it fails to find valid ground. Rewards and crates use their own loot tables.

### Appearance, mutations and individual size

| Trait | Roll | Income | Base speed | Sleep HP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | 96.05% | ×1  | +0% | ×1  |
| Gold | 3%  | ×3  | +5% | ×1.5 |
| Diamond | 0.8% | ×8  | +10% | ×2.2 |
| Rainbow | 0.15% | ×25 | +15% | ×3.5 |
| Volted | 12% per eligible storm check | ×2  | +5% | ×1.3 |

**Normal** has no extra multiplier and accounts for **96.05%** of ordinary appearance rolls. Gold, Diamond and Rainbow are alternative appearances. Volted is a separate storm mutation and can stack with an appearance. The speed bonuses from appearance and mutation are added together before the body and speed formulas. Cash and Sleep HP multipliers stack by multiplication. A rare **2%** size roll gives a Huge body of **1.35–1.50×**. Other size rolls are clustered near 1.0× and clamped to **0.75–1.35×**. Individual wild weight also rolls around **0.90–1.10×**. A large or variant catch can need noticeably more darts than its roster baseline.

sections.title: Day, night, storms and parties
sections.markdown:
The game clock starts with the server. Check the day or night counter when planning a catch or waiting for recovery.

-   A full day/night cycle runs **10 minutes** per animal year. Day lasts 7 minutes and night lasts 3. Night shrinks wildlife detection to 75% and speeds ranch recovery to 10×.
-   At most one biome has an active storm. The first storm starts after roughly 4–9 minutes. Later gaps are 8–18 minutes and storms last 3–5 minutes. The weather tile names the active habitat.
-   **Volted** has a 12% chance on an eligible new wild spawn in a storm, with additional 12% checks about once per minute on existing eligible awake wildlife. Already-mutated animals keep their mutation. Recovery and carry times are separate mechanics.
-   An owner-started **Admin Abuse Party** is announced in that server. Its active modifiers are **2× ranch Cash**, a **50% higher population target** and extra Legendary chances. Its first extra spawn is due shortly after the party starts and then about every 15 minutes. The generic event list in the reviewed world module is empty.

**Recovery example.** Two minutes of remaining recovery work takes about 12 seconds in a stable night window. With the permanent recovery perk it takes about 3 seconds. A switch back to day rescales the remaining time. Hunts still use the separate carry clock.

sections.title: Grassland
sections.markdown:
**Open to everyone.** Meadows, broadleaf trees and grass-topped rock or soil terraces lead out from the hub. Start close to the brick edge. sections.title: Pet levels, weight and earnings
sections.markdown:
A pet card shows several traits. **Rarity** sets its baseline and level ceiling, **appearance** is Normal/Gold/Diamond/Rainbow, and **Volted** can appear beside any appearance. Pets also have individual size and weight, age, feeding XP and paid stat points. The atlas lists standard size-1, weight-roll-1 specimens with zero age, XP and upgrades.

| Rarity | Max level | Total XP | XP per level | Speed cap | Size cap | Jump / Earn cap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Common | 10  | 4,500 | 500 | 30  | 30  | 30  |
| Uncommon | 20  | 9,500 | 500 | 60  | 60  | 60  |
| Rare | 40  | 20,000 | 512.82 | 60  | 100 | 120 |
| Epic | 60  | 40,000 | 677.97 | 60  | 100 | 180 |
| Legendary | 80  | 70,000 | 886.08 | 60  | 100 | 240 |
| Mystic | 100 | 100,000 | 1,010.1 | 60  | 100 | 300 |

| Purchased stat | Per point | Limits and use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Speed | +0.5% to the speed multiplier | Up to 60 points, subject to level. A full Common can buy 30 points. Very high final speeds taper toward the 300 stud/s cap. |
| Jump | +0.1% to mount JumpPower | Base JumpPower 85. Level cap applies. |
| Size | +1 percentage point of growth | Up to 100 points. Visual growth adds size in five 10% steps, capped at 1.5× the species scale in the shared growth formula. |
| Earn | +0.3% to the base income multiplier | Level cap applies. Earn and Speed are the most expensive tracks for a given pet. |

XP needed per level is the rarity's total XP divided by **max level − 1**. Cash points cost more as you add points to a track. For the next point the code starts from the greater of 100 Cash or 25.5 seconds of that pet's base income, then applies track price weight, prior points and the habitat price scale. Track weights are Speed 5, Jump 1, Size 2 and Earn 5. The shop rounds the result. Food and upgrades have independent jobs.

**Age and size.** Placed and ridden pets age during active play. Placed pets also age offline. Every 600 seconds of age shows as one animal year, up to 2,000. Natural growth updates in 10-year steps. Growth combines age, the Size track and any legacy growth already recorded in the save. Effective weight scales with the cube of size. Higher relative weight can help an owned mount’s speed. A heavier-than-normal sleeping catch can slow the person carrying it.

**Passive Cash.** An awake placed pet earns its base rate × 1.2 balance boost × rebirth multiplier × (1 + Friend Boost) × permanent multipliers, including the Index boost. An active party can double total ranch payout. A recovering placed pet earns half. A stored pet and a pet you are riding earn no passive Cash from that slot. On a fresh profile, a just-awake size-1 Grassland Common with no other boosts illustrates the baseline at **$6/s**. Catching it also builds Index completion, so your actual HUD may be slightly higher.

**Selling.** A standard size-1, weight-roll-1 Grassland Common has a **$600** sale baseline. The price follows the species income ladder, 120 seconds of baseline, individual capture size, initial weight roll and appearance/mutation income factors. Age, upgrades, personal wealth, rebirth, friend and perk multipliers do not raise it. A Rare-or-higher pet, a pet with special looks or mutation, or an individual priced at $100,000 or more asks for confirmation.

sections.title: Use a radar and manage Wood
sections.markdown:
Hold a radar from Bag or the hotbar and click or tap the world. For Common through Legendary, choose a biome with that rarity currently available. A **Mystic Radar** searches across biomes. Follow the arrow and distance indicator toward the target. A radar gives you a location, while your character still needs the correct gate unlocked to travel there.

-   Only one radar can run. Turn the current one off before selecting a different rarity.
-   A scan starts with **5 minutes**. If you pick up the marked pet, its tracking clock pauses during the carry.
-   The matching radar is spent when an eligible catch is delivered. If another player catches the target, the radar shuts off and stays in your inventory. A timeout with no delivery also keeps it.
-   A target can disappear or move. If there's no eligible target, check the biome selection and the rare-animal status later. The hidden Unlimited Radar entry is a legacy perk.

sections.title: Index, invites and codes
sections.markdown:
### Animal Index

Encountered pets can be marked seen. Catch or receive a species to count it as owned in the collection record. The Index remembers discoveries after a sale. It shows Normal, Gold, Diamond and Rainbow. The Normal count advances with the first capture of that species in any appearance, while the color categories need their own recorded variant. Volted is tracked separately.

| Index tab | Permanent Cash boost for each species recorded in that tab | At 72 entries |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal | +0.5% | +36% |
| Gold | +1% | +72% |
| Diamond | +2% | +144% |
| Rainbow | +4% | +288% |

These contributions add to a theoretical maximum **+540%**, equivalent to **6.4×** before the other multipliers. The Index's dramatic “1 in N” labels are flavor text. The wild refill uses weights and schedules, and paid crates show their own exact odds. Every four unique species opens a Cash claim, up to **18 milestones**. [See all milestone floors](#index-reference).

### Friends and invitations

Every verified Roblox friend currently in the same server adds **+25%** to passive Cash, counted up to ten friends. Their contribution ends when they leave. The six authored plots make the theoretical cap higher than the number of friends that can ordinarily share a six-player ranch server. Separately, a distinct friend whose Roblox join credits your invite advances the Invite boxes. The four claim thresholds are **1 → Epic, 2 → Epic, 3 → Legendary, 4 → Legendary**. Invite claims and Friend Boost are counted independently.

### Redeem codes

Open **Rewards → Codes**, enter a code, and choose **Redeem**. Codes shown here were configured in the inspected build. The server accepts one redemption per player, ignores case and removes whitespace before lookup.

sections.markdown:
Open **Shop** and choose the crate. Buy **1, 3 or 10 rolls** where the offer is available. Each roll grants one pet, with the probabilities below. The Wild Crate mixes the habitats. Each regional crate takes all six listed outcomes from that biome. The ordinary Mystic chance is **1% per roll**. On the **100th roll since the last Mystic for the same crate**, the roll is guaranteed to be that crate's Mystic. Any Mystic from that crate resets that crate's counter. The tracker is saved across sessions and packs.

One outcome per roll. Pity can replace the ordinary roll with the Mystic in the 1% column. Prices above are in Robux.

**Delivery.** Crate pets are granted in their normal appearance with the built-in size roll. They go into a free pen slot or storage, and are ready to use without recovery. Paid random items are unavailable if the per-player policy check disallows them or cannot confirm eligibility. The pity counter applies only to that crate. A wild Legendary or Mystic spawn follows its own schedule.

### Offline earnings

When you return after at least 30 seconds away with placed animals, the game calculates the absence using up to **24 hours** at **50%** of the eligible ranch rate. The calculation ages those placed pets, uses their fully recovered payout rate and the profile's normal permanent multipliers, and omits Friend Boost. Only positive earnings create a claim. In **Welcome back!**, choose **Claim 1×** for free or the paid **Claim 2×**. The paid double path waits for the Roblox receipt. Keep earners placed before you leave.

sections.title: Getting started and capture FAQ
sections.markdown:
### Where do I get my starter money?

Open **Rewards → Missions** and claim both welcome cards. The gifts are $10,000 and 100 Wood. The Dart Pistol costs $5,000 and the Baseball Bat costs 20 Wood during the guided route. Skipping supplies the eligible welcome gifts and missing starter tools.

### What do I do first after the tutorial?

Fill your pen with pets you can bring back reliably. Claim available free rewards, check which pet Rebirth needs, and build up a Wood reserve with a starter melee tool.

### Why are my darts missing?

Keep the animal in the crosshair, close the gap if it is out of range, and move clear of rocks, tree trunks and terrain. You and the target must be in the target's home biome. Lower ground can also help if the cliff-guard message appears.

### Is there an Auto Aim button?

The current HUD removed Auto Aim and its T shortcut. Aim through the center crosshair and scope manually.

### How do I make the gun stronger?

Open **Upgrade → Guns**, choose a gun you own, and buy its Sleep DMG points. Upgrades belong to that gun. Buy Ammo, Reload or Scope when those are the limits you keep running into.

### Why does my gun put one Fox to sleep faster than another?

The atlas shows a size-1 Normal baseline. A bigger body, special appearance or a Volted mutation can increase Sleep HP. Upgrades on the gun change how much each landed hit contributes.

### Why can't I pick up a sleeping animal?

Get closer and wait for the pickup prompt. Another player's claim starts with a five-second window. An animal can wake, be picked up by someone else, or be out of reach from where you stand.

### Can I pick up from a mount?

Yes, if you are close enough for the pickup prompt. The mounting case uses the mount's size to adjust the reach, and the normal capture checks still apply.

### Where does the carry timer stop?

At the paved hub boundary. Walk further into your own enclosure to finish claiming the pet. Watch for the **Safe!** and then the capture notifications.

### Can I drop it to help a friend?

Dropping a wild sleeper puts it on a pickup timer. Claim protection and ownership rules still apply. A knocked-loose carry has no normal protection. The game has no regular direct pet-trading menu in the reviewed player flow.

### Can someone steal a pet from my pen?

The theft mechanic concerns a sleeping wild catch being carried in the wild. An already-owned enclosure pet is protected.

### What if I leave while holding a catch?

An undelivered wild pet is lost when you leave. Carry it into the enclosure before quitting if you want to keep it.

### Why is my pet doing nothing in the Bag?

Stored pets are safe inventory. Earnings require a placed pet. **Ranch → Place Best** can bring your best earners into the pen.

sections.title: Ranch, riding and logging FAQ
sections.markdown:
### Why is a new pet earning half?

It is recovering from the wild capture. Keep it placed and let it wake. Night speeds recovery, and the permanent perk stacks with night.

### Can feeding wake a pet?

Food adds XP. The recovery timer, night bonus, recovery perk and Wake Now use a separate system.

### Can a Common pet keep leveling forever?

Common pets top out at level 10 and 4,500 XP. Mystic pets top out at level 100 and 100,000 XP. See all six ceilings in [Pet levels](#pet-math).

### Why can I see an upgrade but can't buy it?

Check the wallet, level and track cap. Animal and gun tracks use Cash. Melee tracks use Wood. Feeding increases pet XP and opens additional room for stat points.

### Where did my pet go after riding?

It becomes a held animal when you dismount. Click or tap inside your own enclosure to place it, or use its card where the place action is shown.

### Can every pet fly?

Four can fly in this roster. They are Griffin, Sand Dragon, Dragon and Violet Wyvern. The other two Mystics, Cerberus and Yeti, stay on the ground.

### Why can't I dismount right now?

The driver needs to be grounded. Descend or use **Land**, then select **Dismount**. A passenger can leave using their passenger action or Jump.

### Why does my mount turn transparent when I aim?

The current HUD automatically fades a mount if its body blocks your crosshair in gun mode. Other players still see the mount. Scoping can hide the rider and mount on your own screen.

### Can two people ride one pet?

Yes. One drives and one uses **Ride along**. Board while the mount is grounded and the rear seat is free.

### Do trees use up my bat?

Melee tools are owned equipment. Use the same one repeatedly. Higher tiers and Tree DMG upgrades make later trees easier to fell.

### Why isn't Auto Chop doing anything?

Take out your melee tool, switch Auto Chop on, face an eligible tree and get close enough. Wait if the target is still a stump. Menus, being down and carrying a wild pet can prevent a swing.

### Does Auto Chop collect every tree in the biome?

It checks for a reachable trunk ahead. Your tool's sweep and cleave determine what the actual swing can hit. Move manually to new spots.

### Which trees are worth the most Wood?

Golden trees give five times their normal base amount. Reference base yield rises from 2 Wood in the Grassland to 150 in Enchanted Grove before boosters. Taller individuals can pay more.

### Do melee hits take a player's health?

The system is built around knockback and ragdolls. A player can lose a carried sleeper outside the safe zone if they get hit.

sections.title: Rebirth, wildlife and rewards FAQ
sections.markdown:
### Do I lose my animals when I rebirth?

The currency route resets Cash and pays the Wood cost. The required pet and the rest of your collection stay. The Robux skip keeps your balance too.

### Does my next required animal change if I rejoin?

The requirement is saved for that stage. Look at **Rebirth**. Any owned specimen of the requested species, placed or stored, qualifies.

### Why won't this gate open?

Check its rebirth number. The order is Grassland, Savanna, Snowland, Desert, Prehistoric, Enchanted Grove. The final enclosure requires one more stage after Enchanted opens.

### Does a stronger mount let me skip a gate?

The same gate restrictions apply to ground movement and flying. Rebirth to gain access.

### Where is the Legendary or Mystic that just spawned?

The ordinary announcement leaves out its biome. Check the relevant radar and the HUD. Common through Legendary scans ask for a biome. Mystic searches all biomes.

### Why did my radar turn off and stay in Bag?

A timeout or another player's capture can end the scan without spending it. Successful delivery of a matching tracked catch spends the radar.

### Why didn't I see a rare spawn as soon as the timer hit zero?

Scheduling is per server. Finding valid spawn ground can fail, and a Mystic already alive prevents another scheduled Mystic. The timer also rotates between rarity labels.

### Can Volted and Rainbow appear together?

Yes. Rainbow is an appearance and Volted is a mutation. A wild pet can have both. See [Spawns and weather](#wildlife) for the separate rolls.

### Do the Index labels show exact wild odds?

The Index's “1 in N” values are flavor. Base wildlife uses species selection weights and caps, scheduled rarities use timers, and paid crates list probabilities for each outcome.

### Can I claim the next daily reward if I missed yesterday?

Yes. The next claim advances one slot after UTC midnight. Skipping a day does not reset the calendar.

### Why does another player have different daily missions?

The game picks three from the same pool for each player and UTC day. Quests are persistent and have the same thresholds.

sections.title: Shopping and troubleshooting FAQ
sections.markdown:
### Where are the older gift bundles, pet displays and global Dart Levels?

The current Shop hides legacy Starter, Rider, Pro, Unlimited Radar and the old dart pack. Current premium pets come through crates and ordinary reward/capture paths. Dart stats now belong to the individual gun. Older snapshots can show different menus.

### Why does a Robux button say Coming soon?

The server only enables a configured prompt when Roblox returns an expected product or pass price. A missing, unavailable or mismatched product can leave the button disabled.

### Why are crates unavailable for me?

The game checks Roblox's eligibility result for paid random items. If eligibility cannot be established, the purchase flow remains unavailable.

### Can I get pets without Robux?

Yes. Capture wild animals and claim eligible daily, invite and quest rewards. Some later prizes and premium options are simply additional routes.

### When does a gift arrive?

A player in your server may receive it after the purchase clears. Gifts to friends elsewhere can be queued. Keep the purchase details if delivery fails so the owner can trace the grant.

### What if I already own a perk somebody sends?

The purchase flow tries to detect it before charging. A duplicate that arrives afterward can be credited as Cash according to the store's fallback logic.

### Why wasn't I paid offline?

Check that animals were placed and you were away for at least 30 seconds. The **Welcome back!** card appears with a positive claim. A pet left stored after a ride is outside the placed roster.

### How do I quiet the experience?

Use **Settings** for Music, Sound effects, Full effects, Camera shake, Animal name tags and Tree hit flash. Roblox's Reduce Motion option also reduces decorative animation. The settings described here are wired in the current source.

### Why is the loading bar near 99%?

The client may still be waiting for the world, profile, original assets, terrain near spawn, or the character. The loading-screen **Skip** dismisses the visual overlay while the underlying readiness checks continue. If the loader reports a failure, use its retry action if shown or rejoin. Loading-screen Skip and tutorial Skip are separate buttons.

### Where do I report a bug?

Use the hub's **Feedback** stand. Include the biome, what you pressed, what happened and the exact message if there was one. Use a short note and leave out payment credentials or personal contact details.

sections.title: Source of truth and verification
sections.markdown:
### Reviewed build

-   Source came from the open version **260** Studio place. The inventory indicated streaming on, six placed plot pads, six biome template packs, 72 animal templates, 15 dart gun templates, 13 melee templates and 12 décor templates.
-   The study inventoried **569 Luau containers** across the inspected services and copied **101 gameplay, UI and world-generation source units** into a private working folder. Many of the remaining containers are asset metadata or placement data. The place scripts were read in place, then analyzed on local copies.
-   The catalogs use **ReplicatedStorage.WR.Config**, **WR.Species** and **WR.Calc**. The shared number tables were evaluated locally in Luau, with minimal stand-ins for Roblox data types. The shipped mathematical assertions executed. The generator also checked the exact 72/15/13 counts, one local rig and picture per species, 30 daily rewards, and seven crate probability totals.
-   A brief local Studio run reached server **GameReady / READY** and the client created its game HUD. The only image taken in that run and used here is the loading screen. Studio was already closed when the stop request reached it. This review did not reopen or restart Studio after that point. Local project images supply the gameplay and model pictures in this guide.
-   Full end-to-end play, concurrent competition and ride-along, physical mobile and controller behavior, hosted file delivery, saved progress and real Roblox purchases were not exercised on this build. Current instructions for those mechanics come from the source paths below.

### What can be older than the current build?

The networked game boots from **WRServer.Main** and its **WR** shared tables. The place still has some **Wildshot** helpers used by movement and visual presentation, legacy shared configuration, builds in ServerStorage and archived models. Use the current entry-point dependencies for balance and feature availability. Some source comments and archived screens still say “free” for tutorial purchases, show shorter rare timers, show Auto Aim, or have an E prompt for dismount. Version 260's active paths win those discrepancies.

### Support evidence to request

For loading or save incidents, record the build, exact message, rough time and whether the player made it into a server. For capture, include biome, gun, target and whether there was a clear line of sight. For paid products, record the product and Roblox purchase reference through a private support channel. The public feedback text is filtered and intended for short notes.

sections.title: How the game is wired
sections.markdown:
| Responsibility | Studio source names | What it owns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start and prepare assets | `WRServer.Main`, `WorldBuild`, `GunBuild`, `HubBuild`, `WRLoading` | Boot states, saved world and weapon validation, interaction prompts and readiness. |
| Shared balance | `WR.Config`, `WR.Species`, `WR.Calc` | Active catalogs, stats, pricing and rules shared between server and display. |
| Wildlife and captures | `World`, `Wildlife`, `Session`, `Rig` | Cycle, storms, ordinary and scheduled animals, sedation, carry, ownership and income. |
| Ranch and mounts | `Ranch`, `Enclosure`, `Riding`, client `Mount` and `Animals` | Plot assignment, pet state, poses, flight, passengers, placement and décor. |
| Lumber and knockback | `Chop`, `Melee`, `Ragdoll` | Eligible swings, damage to trees, shared wood, regrowth, knocks and immunity. |
| Store and social | `Shop`, `Market`, `Purchases`, `Store`, `Social`, `Rewards` | Market purchases, crates, Robux receipts, gifts, leaderboards, invites and reward claims. |
| Player interface | `WRClient.Hud`, `Panels`, `PanelsAnimals`, `PanelsMeta`, `PanelsShops` | Hotbar, scope controls, cash/wood, selection, maps, rewards and settings. |
| Persistence and communication | `Data`, `Net`, `Tutorial`, `Admin` | Live profile leases, validated and throttled gameplay requests, welcome checkpoints and feedback. |

### Startup and visuals

The server first validates the permanent weapon templates and the saved terrain/world assets against a hosted release manifest. It preserves the saved layout and creates interaction extras where needed. The runtime systems then start and load player profiles. The loading client watches world and player readiness, gives optional asset preload progress, and can show a retry or rejoin message if required startup fails. The server follows the saved asset paths rather than generating the whole place every join.

The active world presentation uses biome and time-of-day lighting and music, transition effects, local weather, player and pet animation, and replicated hit and recovery cues. The Animal Rig Lab template is wrapped in a gameplay rig with a collision body so the source visual can animate. The HUD draws temporary notifications, sedate bars, rarity highlights, radar cues, carrying VFX and reward animations. Viewports reuse game models for pet and equipment cards. The user can tone down sound, effects, shake, flash and labels. There is a separate preference for Auto Chop.

sections.title: Saves, receipts and compatibility
sections.markdown:
The live profile has a server lease, periodic autosave, release and shutdown handling. The source autosaves roughly every **60 seconds** and uses a **30-minute** stale-lease threshold. Active lease or load trouble can block a join rather than create a new replacement profile. Captures, sales and confirmed rewards have prompt save paths. Studio play uses temporary profiles. The current save reader repairs only affected fields where possible, keeping unknown legacy data for recovery.

A profile covers wallets and lifetime counters, tutorial, rebirth stage and requirement, weapons and individual upgrades, animals and placements, decorations, Bag and hotbar, Index discoveries, rewards, radar and food inventory, social claims, settings, perks, gifts, receipt ledger and per-crate pity. The board uses separate ordered totals for lifetime Cash, lifetime Wood and played time. The Wood column’s lifetime total can include qualifying Wood rewards and paid packs as well as chopped Wood. An open carry and current world wildlife belong to the session.

Developer products use one receipt dispatcher. The server verifies configured prices for UI visibility, tracks purchase IDs, saves a grant before acknowledging a live receipt where the normal path succeeds, and retries unavailable profiles or saves. Gift redemption has a recipient queue. Some products remember their immediate target in session state. For example, a late Wake Now receipt can choose the longest remaining placed recovery if its original target is unavailable. Verify late and cancel cases when testing monetization.

### Compatibility details

-   Old global darts and retired sharpening had migration/refund logic. Earlier gun and melee inventories use tier remaps. The active player path is per item.
-   An older Phoenix pet is mapped to Sand Dragon. Phoenix is not in the version 260 roster, and the archive still contains Phoenix assets.
-   Enchanted display names were updated while keeping the old IDs so owned pets, model lookup and crate entries stay associated.
-   The owner panel contains private test and live-event controls. Ordinary players use the published player UI. The feedback inbox, owner QA and admin actions have separate owner checks.

sections.title: Reference math and timings
sections.markdown:
| Quantity | How the reviewed game computes it |
| --- | --- |
| Wild sleep threshold | Reference entry gun's power × rarity coefficient (2.6, 4.2, 6.6, 10.2, 16.2 or 25.5) × capture size^1.5 × applicable appearance and mutation HP factors. |
| Hits to sleep | Smallest whole number of landed hits whose total Sleep DMG meets the threshold. A Normal size-1 animal takes 3, 5, 7, 11, 17 or 26 hits at its biome's entry gun base power. |
| Wake clock | 4 sec + distance / (reference travel pace × carry speed factor) × margin. Margin starts at 1.14, then drops by 0.008 per rarity step and 0.01 per special appearance step. |
| Carry speed factor | 0.97 at normal relative weight, then about 0.073 less per doubling above normal, bounded at 0.75. Subsequent travel pace includes the current mount or walking speed. |
| Base passive Cash/s | 5 × habitat income ladder × 1.75^rarity step × capture size^1.5 × (1 + 1.5 × growth) × trait income × Earn stat multiplier. Ordinary habitat step is 2.5×. Legendary/Mystic are anchored at the last biome and step back at 2.25×. |
| Effective kg | Species kg × drawn size^3 × individual weight factor. The physics rig can have its own species-scale adjustments. |
| Recovery base seconds | Round(120 × 45^((biome index − 1 + 2 × rarity step) ÷ 15)). Divide remaining work by the active 1×, 4×, 10× or 40× rate to estimate the visible timer. |
| Growth fraction | Capped at 1. Combines natural growth ((age rounded down to 10-year step) / 2,000)^0.8, legacy food growth and 0.01 per Size point. |
| Rarity / weapon ordering | Rarity step is 0 for Common through 5 for Mystic. Entry guns for biomes 1–6 are tiers 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11. Upgraded power is quantized to 1/256. |
| Index claim | The greater of the configured floor and full-rate eligible ranch income × 60 × (3 + the smaller of milestone number and 9). |

The tables use current calculations for the ordinary baseline. Visual pose, individual size, variant, clock and equipped stats can change what the player sees. Travel distance here is planar distance from pickup to the enclosure center. The actual safe line stops the carry earlier than the center when you approach it normally.
